newsitem.title: UK: BTPs, Bonos worst hit in dire week for debt - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: BTPs, Bonos worst hit in dire week for debt - Salomon.

text.p: Italian and Spanish bonds suffered worst in an overwhelmingly negative week for bond markets, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.
Swiss bonds were the only ones to show a positive return in local currency terms, gaining 0.49 percent in the week ended Thursday. The overall index, comprising 16 major markets, fell 0.24 percent.

Italian BTPs shed 1.10 percent during the week while Spanish Bonos lost 0.98 percent. Analysts said market speculation that European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) might be delayed took its toll most on these two markets.

U.S. Treasuries were shaken by market talk that U.S. interest rates might have to rise amid the view that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan was taking a more hawkish stance. But in the end they lost just 0.10 percent.
But not all dollar bloc debt proved so resilient. Australian bonds lost 0.82 percent in local currency terms, the third-worst performance in the week.

The U.S. dollar staged another week of impressive gains, making most markets' returns even worse in dollar terms. The three main "high yielder" markets in Europe -- Sweden, Italy and Spain -- made the biggest losses for dollar-based investors.
Sweden, which lost 0.44 percent in Swedish crowns, shed 2.69 percent in dollars. Italian bonds lost 2.50 percent and Spanish bonds were down 2.21 percent.

Of the 16 markets, only three finished the week in positive territory. Japanese government bonds made a 0.46 percent gain, Swiss bonds returned 0.18 percent and Australian debt made a 0.12 percent return.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
